cues.en: The other day I cycled 14 kilometers.
cues.zh: 前几天我骑了14公里。

cues.en: And the next day 27.
cues.zh: 第二天骑了27公里。

cues.en: And the day after that I walked three kilometers.
cues.zh: 再下一天我步行了三公里。

cues.en: None of this was particularly notable and I didn't really consider it exercise
cues.zh: 这些都不算什么特别的事，我也没真的把它当作锻炼。

cues.en: either.
cues.zh: 也没当回事。

cues.en: It's just part of living in a walkable, bikeable city. What I like to call the gym of life.
cues.zh: 这只是生活在一座适合步行和骑行的城市的一部分。我喜欢称之为“生活健身房”。

cues.en: I'm not the kind of person who enjoys exercising.
cues.zh: 我不是那种喜欢锻炼的人。

cues.en: Playing sports and going to the gym has never really interested me. Just ask my brother. Haven't we done this joke already?
cues.zh: 运动、去健身房从来都不太吸引我。问问我兄弟就知道了。这个梗我们是不是已经玩过了？

cues.en: But that's really not that unusual. Right? Because the majority of people are not gym people.
cues.zh: 但这其实没什么不寻常的，对吧？因为大多数人并不是健身房爱好者。

cues.en: Anybody who goes to the gym regularly knows never to go in the first few weeks of January because it'll be full of all the New Year's Resolutioners.
cues.zh: 任何经常去健身房的人都知道，一月份的头几周千万别去，因为那里会挤满新年决心党。

cues.en: By March, at the latest, the gym is nearly empty again.
cues.zh: 最迟到三月，健身房就又几乎空了。

cues.en: The business model of gyms literally depends on most people not going. But exercise is important.
cues.zh: 健身房的商业模式实际上就是靠大多数人不来。但锻炼很重要。

cues.en: Human beings were not meant to sit in little cubicles staring at computer screens all day filling out useless forms and
cues.zh: 人类本来就不该整天坐在小隔间里盯着电脑屏幕填那些没用的表格，

cues.en: wait, I've done this joke before too.
cues.zh: 等等，这个梗我之前也玩过了。

cues.en: But anyway, being sedentary is unnatural for us, and it brings with it a lot of health problems.
cues.zh: 不管怎样，久坐对我们来说是不自然的，它会带来很多健康问题。

cues.en: Problems that are easily avoidable with even a small amount of daily exercise.
cues.zh: 这些问题只要每天做少量运动就能轻松避免。

cues.en: But the reality is that a majority of people don't get enough exercise each day.
cues.zh: 但现实是，大多数人每天都没有得到足够的运动。

cues.en: A recent study by Stanford University tracked the daily activity levels of over 700,000
cues.zh: 斯坦福大学最近的一项研究追踪了超过70万人的日常活动水平，

cues.en: people across 46 countries.
cues.zh: 这些人分布在46个国家。

cues.en: They found that the average person in The United States,
cues.zh: 研究发现，美国普通人

cues.en: Canada,
cues.zh: 加拿大、

cues.en: Australia,
cues.zh: 澳大利亚、

cues.en: and New Zealand walked less than 5,000
cues.zh: 和新西兰人每天步行不到5000

cues.en: steps per day,
cues.zh: 步，

cues.en: the lowest in the developed world.
cues.zh: 是发达国家中最低的。

cues.en: So why is that?
cues.zh: 那这是为什么呢？

cues.en: Well, this study showed a direct correlation between walkability
cues.zh: 这项研究显示，步行便利性与

cues.en: and the average amount of steps of the people who live there.
cues.zh: 当地居民的平均步数之间存在直接关联。

cues.en: Put simply, European cities are, on average, more walkable than cities in The US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand. And so the average European
cues.zh: 简单来说，欧洲城市平均比美国、加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰的城市更适合步行。因此，欧洲人平均

cues.en: gets more exercise
cues.zh: 能从生活这座健身房里

cues.en: from the gym of life.
cues.zh: 获得更多锻炼。

cues.en: But even within these countries,
cues.zh: 但即便在这些国家内部，

cues.en: not all cities are equal.
cues.zh: 城市之间也并不相同。

cues.en: As you might expect, they found a huge difference between the average number of steps between different US cities,
cues.zh: 正如你所料，他们发现美国不同城市之间的平均步数差异巨大，

cues.en: which directly correlated to how walkable they are.
cues.zh: 而这与城市的步行便利性直接相关。

cues.en: Of course, this is not a new discovery.
cues.zh: 当然，这并不是什么新发现。

cues.en: Multiple studies have shown that people in walkable cities walk more than people in car dependent places. And, yeah, that's kinda obvious.
cues.zh: 多项研究已经表明，步行便利城市的人比依赖汽车地区的人走得更多。嗯，这挺显而易见的。

cues.en: You're a lot more likely to walk in a place like this
cues.zh: 在这样的地方，你步行的可能性

cues.en: than a place like this.
cues.zh: 远比在这样的地方大得多。

cues.en: In the 2004 documentary
cues.zh: 在2004年的纪录片

cues.en: Supersize Me, the author tries to go thirty days while eating only McDonald's food and walking as much as the average American.
cues.zh: 《超级汉堡王》中，作者尝试连续三十天只吃麦当劳，并像普通美国人一样步行。

cues.en: He quickly found out that he could not walk so little while living in New York City. All I did today was leave my apartment,
cues.zh: 他很快发现，住在纽约市根本没法走那么少。我今天就只是离开公寓、

cues.en: walk down the stairs, and walk to the McDonald's.
cues.zh: 下楼，然后走到麦当劳。

cues.en: steps. He completed the last part of the experiment in Houston where it's much easier to avoid walking.
cues.zh: 步。他在休斯顿完成了实验的最后部分，在那里避开步行要容易得多。

cues.en: I was curious to see what my step count was, so I bought one of those fancy time bracelets that tracks your,
cues.zh: 我很好奇自己的步数是多少，就买了那种 fancy 的智能手环来追踪，

cues.en: fitness stuff.
cues.zh: 健身数据。

cues.en: It turns out that I'm unable to get less than about 10,000 steps in a typical day living here in Amsterdam.
cues.zh: 结果发现，在阿姆斯特丹生活，我一天基本上走不到一万步以下。

cues.en: I'd have to go really out of my way to get less than 5,000.
cues.zh: 要想少于五千步，我得特意绕远路才行。

cues.en: As you might expect, the Stanford study also showed a direct correlation between walkability and obesity in the location study.
cues.zh: 正如你所料，斯坦福的研究还显示，在位置研究中，步行便利性与肥胖率之间存在直接关联。

cues.en: Or, to be more precise, they actually found that more walkable places correlated to reduced obesity for everyone,
cues.zh: 或者更准确地说，他们实际上发现，步行便利性更高的地方与所有人肥胖率降低相关，

cues.en: but some groups benefited much more than others, and in fact they called activity inequality.
cues.zh: 但某些群体的受益远大于其他群体，事实上他们称之为活动不平等。

cues.en: Which is really interesting and you can read more about it in the paper itself, which is linked in the description.
cues.zh: 这真的很有趣，你可以在论文本身中读到更多内容，链接在描述中。

cues.en: Because, yeah, if you live here and are wealthy enough, in terms of both time and money, to go to the gym regularly,
cues.zh: 因为，没错，如果你住在这里，并且在时间和金钱上都足够富裕，能定期去健身房，

cues.en: you can beat the average number of steps.
cues.zh: 你就能超过平均步数。

cues.en: But in walkable places,
cues.zh: 但在步行便利的地方，

cues.en: everyone benefits, regardless of their gender or socioeconomic
cues.zh: 每个人都能受益，无论他们的性别或社会经济

cues.en: status.
cues.zh: 状况如何。

cues.en: Now, of course, walkability is not the only reason for obesity or even the most important one.
cues.zh: 当然，步行便利性并不是肥胖的唯一原因，甚至不是最重要的原因。

cues.en: A lack of sidewalks can't fully explain why The US is way the hell up here.
cues.zh: 缺乏人行道不能完全解释为什么美国远远高居这里。

cues.en: But if you want any hope of tackling the obesity crisis, you're going to have to get people moving more often.
cues.zh: 但如果你想有希望解决肥胖危机，就必须让人们更频繁地动起来。

cues.en: I've lived and worked in a lot of different cities, and that's an understatement.
cues.zh: 我在很多不同的城市生活和工作过，这还是保守的说法。

cues.en: And I've commuted in many different ways.
cues.zh: 我通勤用过很多种方式。

cues.en: At one point in my life, I decided that I didn't want to end up as another lazy miserable suburbanite in an SUV.
cues.zh: 曾经有段时间，我下定决心不想变成又一个开着SUV、懒散又痛苦的郊区人。

cues.en: So I started riding my bike to work and I noticed an immediate improvement in my level of energy.
cues.zh: 于是我开始骑车上班，立刻发现精力水平有了明显提升。

cues.en: It was incredible.
cues.zh: 太不可思议了。

cues.en: Within only a few weeks I had lost weight, I had more energy, and I felt significantly less stressed at the end of the day.
cues.zh: 短短几周内我就减了重，精力更充沛，一天下来压力也小了很多。

cues.en: My mood after a cycling commute was much better too. Well, unless it was one of those mornings where I was run off the road by some lazy miserable suburbanite in an SUV.
cues.zh: 骑车通勤后我的心情也好多了。除非哪天早上被某个开着SUV、懒散又痛苦的郊区人逼得骑出路面。

cues.en: Commuting by car in traffic is pretty miserable. Yeah. You get to sit in your climate controlled cage, but you can't do anything productive, and it just feels like wasted time.
cues.zh: 开车堵在路上通勤挺痛苦的。是啊，你能坐在温控笼子里，但什么有产出的事都做不了，感觉就是浪费时间。

cues.en: So I wasn't really surprised to see that surveys taken during COVID found that most people who walk or cycle to work said they miss their commutes,
cues.zh: 所以看到疫情期间的调查发现，大多数步行或骑车上班的人说他们想念自己的通勤，我并不意外，

cues.en: while almost nobody who drives to work said this.
cues.zh: 而几乎没几个开车上班的人这么说。

cues.en: Because walking or cycling to work actually makes you feel good,
cues.zh: 因为走路或骑车上班确实让你感觉良好，

cues.en: while driving
cues.zh: 而开车

cues.en: doesn't.
cues.zh: 不会。

cues.en: People need approximately 30 of moderate physical activity every day, and that can be achieved by cycling or a brisk walk.
cues.zh: 人每天需要大约30分钟中等强度的身体活动，骑车或快走就能达到。

cues.en: But since this activity is required anyway to maintain a base level of health,
cues.zh: 但既然这项活动本来就是维持基本健康所必需的，

cues.en: there's an argument to be made that the first thirty minutes of, say, your cycling commute are free.
cues.zh: 那就可以说，比如你骑车通勤的前三十分钟是免费的。

cues.en: It's time you'd have to spend exercising anyway, and by doing it during your commute, you're saving that time by multitasking.
cues.zh: 反正你本来就得花时间锻炼，而在通勤时锻炼，就是靠一心二用把这段时间省下来。

cues.en: So if you spend forty minutes commuting by bicycle each day, that means you effectively only spend ten minutes a day exclusively on your commute.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你每天骑自行车通勤四十分钟，那就意味着你实际上每天只专门花了十分钟在通勤上。

cues.en: A car commute does not provide this benefit. You're not getting any exercise, so it's just purely time wasted commuting.
cues.zh: 开车通勤没有这个好处。你得不到任何锻炼，所以通勤时间纯粹是浪费。

cues.en: You can't even catch up on work or check your email like you can on a train.
cues.zh: 你甚至不能像坐火车那样顺便处理工作或查邮件。

cues.en: Of course, these benefits aren't available to you if your city is built wrong.
cues.zh: 当然，如果你的城市建得不对，这些好处就享受不到。

cues.en: You can't walk to work if it's too far away, and if there's no rapid transit available to help you get there.
cues.zh: 如果上班地点太远，又没有快速交通能帮你到那里，你就没法步行上班。

cues.en: And you can't cycle anywhere if it's not safe to do so.
cues.zh: 如果骑车不安全，你就哪儿也骑不了。

cues.en: You can, of course, offset this by purposefully getting some exercise by going to the gym or going for a run each morning.
cues.zh: 当然，你可以每天早晨特意去健身房或跑步来锻炼，以此弥补。

cues.en: But it's too easy to skip this. It's too easy to decide one day that you're not in the mood or you don't have enough time.
cues.zh: 但这太容易跳过了。太容易某天决定自己没心情，或者没时间。

cues.en: There are a lot of mornings where I don't want to exercise.
cues.zh: 有很多个早晨，我都不想锻炼。

cues.en: Mornings when I'm tired and worn out, the weather sucks and I just want to get to where I need to go.
cues.zh: 那些早晨，我累得筋疲力尽，天气又糟，我只想赶紧到要去的地方。

cues.en: On these mornings, I hate the walkable city because it forces me to go out into miserable cold and walk or cycle to my destination.
cues.zh: 这种早晨，我讨厌可步行城市，因为它逼我走进讨厌的寒冷里，步行或骑车去目的地。

cues.en: But what inevitably happens is that a few minutes in, I start feeling better. And
cues.zh: 但不可避免的是，过几分钟，我就开始感觉好起来。而且

cues.en: by the time I get to where I'm going, I feel great.
cues.zh: 等我到达目的地时，我感觉棒极了。

cues.en: That miserable feeling that I had in the morning is gone.
cues.zh: 早上那种痛苦的感觉消失了。

cues.en: What's most important though is that once you get over that initial feeling of laziness,
cues.zh: 但最重要的是，一旦你克服了最初的懒惰感，

cues.en: you've now got the energy and motivation to do more.
cues.zh: 你就有了精力和动力去做更多的事。

cues.en: This effect may be part of the reason why a recent Ipsos survey found that people in The Netherlands exercise more than any other nation on Earth.
cues.zh: 这种效应可能部分解释了为什么益普索最近的一项调查发现，荷兰人的运动量比地球上任何其他国家的人都多。

cues.en: Because when you walk or cycle regularly to do everyday activities like shopping, visiting friends, going to appointments, and buying groceries,
cues.zh: 因为当你经常步行或骑车去做日常活动，比如购物、访友、赴约和买菜时，

cues.en: you don't get sucked into that black hole of inactivity.
cues.zh: 你就不会陷入那种久坐不动的黑洞。

cues.en: But this is only possible if your city is designed for it.
cues.zh: 但这只有在你的城市为此而设计的情况下才可能实现。

cues.en: Incidentally,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，

cues.en: I love how in this study The Netherlands had the absolute lowest number of people who reported cycling as a sport they do in a normal week.
cues.zh: 我很喜欢这项研究中的一点：荷兰报告说把骑车作为正常一周内运动项目的人数绝对是最低的。

cues.en: Because the Dutch do not consider this to be a sport.
cues.zh: 因为荷兰人不把这当作一项运动。

cues.en: Only this.
cues.zh: 只有这个才算。

cues.en: They even have different names for both kinds of cyclists.
cues.zh: 他们甚至对这两种骑车人有不同的称呼。

cues.en: Personally, I am a feetser, and I have no interest in being a wheel runner.
cues.zh: 就我个人而言，我是个“步行者”，对当“轮跑者”毫无兴趣。

cues.en: It feels too much like exercising to me. I'm happy with the gym of life.
cues.zh: 对我来说那太像锻炼了。我对生活中的健身房很满意。

cues.en: But regardless of what type you are, cycling is a great low impact aerobic activity that could benefit almost everyone, and making it part of your daily routine can bring immediate health benefits.
cues.zh: 但不管你是哪种类型，骑车都是一项很棒的低冲击有氧运动，几乎人人都能受益，把它融入日常 routine 能带来立竿见影的健康益处。

cues.en: A 2010 study found that the benefits of cycling far outweighed the risks from things like inhaling pollution from cars or being injured or killed by cars.
cues.zh: 2010年的一项研究发现，骑车的好处远远超过了吸入汽车尾气污染或被汽车撞伤撞死等风险。

cues.en: But this study was focused on The Netherlands where cycling is extremely safe.
cues.zh: 但这项研究聚焦于荷兰，那里的骑行非常安全。

cues.en: Car centric cities that are designed wrong are robbing their citizens of this easy low cost opportunity to improve their health.
cues.zh: 以汽车为中心、规划失当的城市，剥夺了居民一个简单又低成本的健康机会。

cues.en: After my dad had knee surgery, he found the very best activity for him was cycling.
cues.zh: 我爸做完膝盖手术后，发现骑车最适合自己。

cues.en: Of course, he needed to get a stationary bike because he lived somewhere car dependent.
cues.zh: 当然，他只能买一辆健身自行车，因为他住在一个离不开汽车的地方。

cues.en: In The Netherlands, he would be able to cycle regularly to do everyday errands and activities like most seniors do here.
cues.zh: 在荷兰，他就能像这里的大多数老年人一样，定期骑车办日常琐事、参加日常活动。

cues.en: And it's possible that with all that daily cycling, he might never have needed that knee surgery in the first place.
cues.zh: 而且，如果每天都骑车，他或许一开始就不需要做膝盖手术。

cues.en: People really underestimate how much a small amount of daily exercise contributes to a better level of physical and mental health.
cues.zh: 人们真的低估了每天少量运动对改善身心健康有多大帮助。

cues.en: And that's what walkable and bikeable cities provide.
cues.zh: 而这正是步行和骑行友好型城市所能带来的。

cues.en: When neighborhoods are mixed use with most of your daily needs within walking distance, you're more likely to take that walk.
cues.zh: 当社区功能混合，大多数日常所需都在步行范围内时，你就更愿意走路。

cues.en: Your kids are more likely to walk or cycle to school.
cues.zh: 你的孩子也更可能步行或骑车上学。

cues.en: And elderly people are much more likely to get the daily exercise they need to stay healthy as they age.
cues.zh: 老年人也更可能获得保持健康、安然老去所需的日常运动。

cues.en: And most importantly,
cues.zh: 最重要的是，

cues.en: everyone is more likely to get that base amount of daily exercise that brings the biggest gain.
cues.zh: 每个人都更有可能获得适量的日常运动，而这能带来最大的收益。

cues.en: Getting out of that pit of laziness that sucks you in physically and mentally so you're better prepared to deal with whatever life throws at you.
cues.zh: 走出那个让人身心都陷入懒散的泥潭，这样你就能更好地应对生活中的种种挑战。

cues.en: I've been all around the world and I firmly believe that walkable places are fundamentally better than car centric places.
cues.zh: 我去过世界各地，坚信适合步行的地方，本质上就比以汽车为中心的地方好。

cues.en: They're just better places to be in and they come with a multitude of benefits for people's health, well-being, the environment, city finances and society as a whole.
cues.zh: 这样的地方住起来就是更舒服，而且对人们的健康、幸福感、环境、城市财政乃至整个社会都有诸多好处。

cues.en: I love walkable cities especially when they're nearly car free, so I've started a series on Nebula about some of the best walkable and low car places in the world.
cues.zh: 我喜欢适合步行的城市，尤其是几乎没有汽车的城市。所以我在 Nebula 上推出了一个系列，介绍世界上一些最适合步行、汽车最少的地方。

cues.en: Nebula is the Streamy award nominated streaming service created by and for educational creators like me.
cues.zh: Nebula 是一个流媒体服务，曾获 Streamy 奖提名，由像我这样的教育类创作者创建，也服务于这类创作者。

cues.en: You'll find all of the videos from YouTube, but also bonus content, extended editions, experimental videos, and podcasts.
cues.zh: 你不仅能看到 YouTube 上的所有视频，还能看到额外内容、加长版、实验性视频和播客。

cues.en: All completely ad free. For example, this ad isn't in the Nebula version of this video.
cues.zh: 而且完全没有广告。比如，这条广告在 Nebula 版视频里就不会出现。

cues.en: I signed up to Nebula ages ago to watch creators like City Beautiful, Legal Eagle, Practical Engineering, and Wendover Productions.
cues.zh: 我很久以前就注册了 Nebula，为的是看 City Beautiful、Legal Eagle、Practical Engineering 和 Wendover Productions 这些创作者的内容。

cues.en: I've really enjoyed Nebula, which is why I wanted my content on there too.
cues.zh: 我真的很喜欢 Nebula，所以也想把自己的内容放上去。

cues.en: By signing up at this link right here, you'll be supporting this channel as well as all the other independent creators you watch on Nebula in the future.
cues.zh: 通过这个链接注册，你既是在支持本频道，也是在支持未来你在 Nebula 上观看的所有独立创作者。

cues.en: I'd also like to thank my supporters on Patreon who pay me to brag about how much exercise I accidentally get. If you'd like your name in this list of supporters, find out more at patreon.com/notchaspikes.
cues.zh: 我还想感谢 Patreon 上的支持者，他们付钱让我吹嘘自己意外获得了多少锻炼机会。如果你也想让自己的名字出现在支持者名单里，可以前往 patreon.com/notchaspikes 了解更多。
